modules.summary: Read the beat and the spaces between beats.

modules.summary: Use 1-e-&-a to decode common rhythmic words.

lessons.title: Find the pulse
lessons.objective: Keep a steady pulse through four measures.
lessons.recallPrompt: Before looking at a line, say: pulse means the steady, evenly spaced beat.
lessons.execution: Clap, or use only the TD-07 snare pad: the large center pad directly in front of you. Strike its center once per numbered beat.

introduces.meaning: a steady series of beats
introduces.target: your hands for clapping, or the TD-07 snare: large center pad
introduces.action: clap or strike the snare center once on each number

steps: Recall what pulse means and point to the snare pad.
Tap four beats and count 1 2 3 4 aloud.
Clap or play the snare once per beat without stopping.

lessons.title: Quarter-note grid
lessons.objective: Read quarter notes and rests in 4/4.
lessons.recallPrompt: Without looking, name ♩ as one sound for one beat and 𝄽 as one silent beat.
lessons.execution: Use the same snare target introduced in lesson 1; strike for ♩ and do not strike for 𝄽.

introduces.meaning: one sound lasting one beat
introduces.action: strike once, then count to the next beat

introduces.meaning: one silent beat
introduces.action: keep counting and do not strike

steps: Recall and name each symbol before the line appears.
Clap the line, including silent rests.
Play the snare only where ♩ appears at 60 BPM.

lessons.title: Count the &
lessons.recallPrompt: Say what ♫ means: two equal sounds inside one numbered beat.
lessons.execution: Stay on the known snare pad; make two even strokes while saying number-and.

introduces.meaning: two equal sounds within one beat, counted number-and
introduces.action: make two even strokes, one on the number and one on &

steps: Recall ♫ and say its count before playing.
Say 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & while tapping.
Play two short lines on snare only.

lessons.title: Hear the silence
lessons.recallPrompt: Say that an eighth rest is silence for half a beat; the count does not stop.
lessons.execution: Use the known snare. Lift or ghost-move the stick for the rest; do not hit any pad.

introduces.meaning: silence for the number or & half of a beat
introduces.action: keep the count moving and make no sound

steps: Recall that silence still has a place in the count.
Count through every rest.
Play snare attacks only where a sound is written.

lessons.title: Change the measure
lessons.recallPrompt: Read 3/4 aloud: three quarter-note beats per measure; the top number is the beats to count.
lessons.execution: Clap or use the familiar snare target; meter changes how far you count before returning to 1, not which pad you hit.

introduces.meaning: how many quarter-note beats are in each measure
introduces.target: the familiar snare or clapping hands
introduces.action: restart the count at 1 after the stated number of beats

steps: Recall the meaning of the top number.
Mark and say the strong first beat.
Play one meter at a time, switching only between lines.

lessons.title: Hold and connect
lessons.objective: Perform ties and dotted values without adding attacks.
lessons.recallPrompt: Say: a tie joins two notes into one attack; a dot adds half of the note's value.
lessons.execution: On the familiar snare, make one attack at a tied group’s start, then count through the held time without a second hit.

introduces.meaning: connects written notes into one continuous duration
introduces.action: strike only at the first tied note

introduces.meaning: adds half of that note’s value
introduces.action: strike once then count the longer duration

steps: Recall tie versus dot before seeing examples.
Circle the actual attacks.
Count held durations, then perform without extra strikes.

lessons.title: Own the offbeat
lessons.recallPrompt: Say: an offbeat is the & between numbered beats, not a new drum.
lessons.execution: Keep the foot on numbered beats and strike the known snare only on written offbeat attacks.

introduces.meaning: the second half of an eighth-note beat
introduces.action: strike precisely on & when a note is written there

steps: Recall what & means.
Tap foot on numbers and clap only written attacks.
Transfer the same attacks to snare without stopping.

lessons.title: Interleaved rhythm set
lessons.recallPrompt: Name quarter note, rest, paired eighths, and offbeat before choosing a line.
lessons.execution: Every line remains a one-surface snare or clap exercise; no new kit target is implied.

introduces.meaning: switching among already learned ideas
introduces.action: identify symbols first, then perform

steps: Recall all symbols before each line.
Preview for 20 seconds and name the counts.
Play each line once and log the error type.

lessons.title: The 1-e-&-a grid
lessons.recallPrompt: Say 1 e & a: four equally spaced places inside one beat.
lessons.execution: Use the established snare target for every written sixteenth; this is a timing lesson, not new kit notation.

introduces.meaning: four equal subdivisions inside one beat
introduces.action: make one even stroke for each written subdivision

steps: Recall the full spoken grid.
Speak it while tapping evenly.
Play selected positions on snare at 50 BPM.

lessons.title: Subdivision changes
lessons.objective: Move between quarters, eighths, and sixteenths.
lessons.recallPrompt: Name the count for one, two, and four sounds in a beat.
lessons.execution: Remain on the known snare target; only the spacing changes.

introduces.meaning: a change in how many equal sounds fit one beat
introduces.action: change spacing while keeping the beat steady

steps: Recall each count before it appears.
Listen for equal spacing.
Change subdivisions on snare only after naming them.

lessons.title: Meet your TD-07 kit map
lessons.objective: Identify each first drum/cymbal symbol, its TD-07 target, and its stroke before reading a groove.
lessons.recallPrompt: For each mark, say symbol → instrument name → physical TD-07 target → playing action before striking it.
lessons.execution: Do not combine parts yet. Identify and play one target at a time, then answer the recall prompt again.

introduces.symbol: ◆ regular note at middle staff position
introduces.meaning: snare drum voice
introduces.action: strike the center with one relaxed stick

introduces.symbol: ● regular note low in the staff
introduces.meaning: bass drum voice
introduces.target: TD-07 kick pedal and kick pad
introduces.action: press the pedal once with the foot

introduces.meaning: closed hi-hat cymbal voice
introduces.action: strike the pad with a relaxed tip stroke; keep the hi-hat pedal down

introduces.meaning: crash cymbal voice
introduces.action: strike once near the edge, then let it ring

introduces.meaning: ride cymbal voice
introduces.action: strike once with a controlled tip stroke

steps: Read the legend aloud: written mark, name, target, and action.
Point to each TD-07 target before striking it alone.
Use the recall check until every mark has an answer, then read single-limb examples.

lessons.title: Layer a groove
lessons.objective: Combine already identified hi-hat, snare, and bass layers.
lessons.recallPrompt: Before each line, point and say × = left hi-hat, ◆ = center snare, ● = kick pedal.
lessons.execution: Build one known target at a time: hi-hat, then bass plus snare, then all three.

introduces.meaning: more than one known kit voice occurring at the same time
introduces.target: the named TD-07 targets from the kit map
introduces.action: prepare each limb, then strike or press together only when marks align

steps: Recall every symbol-to-target pairing.
Play hi-hat alone, then bass and snare alone.
Combine at a slow tempo only after each layer is clean.

lessons.title: Read one beat ahead
lessons.objective: Keep eyes ahead of the current strike.
lessons.recallPrompt: Name every symbol and target in the next beat before playing the current beat.
lessons.execution: Use only targets already introduced in the kit map; if a mark has no known target, stop and return to the legend.

introduces.meaning: previewing upcoming known information before performing it
introduces.action: keep eyes one beat ahead while limbs perform the current beat

steps: Preview and name next-beat landmarks.
Track the next beat with your eyes.
Recover at the next beat after errors.

lessons.title: Unseen reading sets
lessons.objective: Complete three new examples using only previously taught marks and kit targets.
lessons.recallPrompt: Scan first: name every symbol, instrument, TD-07 target, and count you will use.
lessons.execution: Perform only after the scan confirms that every mark has a known meaning and physical target.

introduces.meaning: first-time reading without first-time symbols
introduces.action: scan, name, count, then perform once

steps: Use genuinely new combinations, never unexplained symbols.
Scan and recall before one preview and one performance.
Repeat only once, then move on.

lessons.title: Five landmark pitches
lessons.objective: Map Middle C, treble G/C, and bass F/C.
lessons.recallPrompt: Name each landmark before revealing it and point to its place on the keyboard diagram.
lessons.execution: Use the virtual piano; this separate pitch bridge does not change the TD-07 drum map.

introduces.meaning: a fixed reference note for finding other pitches
introduces.target: matching key on a virtual keyboard
introduces.action: name it, locate it, then play it once

steps: Recall the note name.
Find it on a keyboard diagram.
Draw it from memory.

lessons.title: Read by interval
lessons.objective: Read steps, skips, and repeated notes without mnemonics.
lessons.recallPrompt: Say step, skip, or repeat before moving from one staff note to the next.
lessons.execution: Start from a known keyboard landmark and move to the next key shape; this remains piano-only work.

introduces.symbol: adjacent, skipped, or repeated staff positions
introduces.meaning: the distance and direction between notes
introduces.target: virtual keyboard keys near a known landmark
introduces.action: identify direction and shape before pressing the next key

steps: Name direction first.
Identify step, skip, or repeat.
Play from a landmark note.
